title: Лёва влюбился в Катю  (Lyova Fell in Love with Katya)

segments.t: At the start of a busy morning in the kitchen, Lyova gets distracted watching the Chef's daughter Katya and spills scalding coffee on himself. Max quickly realizes that Lyova has fallen head over heels for her.
Идеальное начало дня — бодрящий душ.
Плотный завтрак и чашечка горячего кофе.
Ой, Лёва, это очень горячо!
Прости меня, пожалуйста, я случайно.
Ты опять за Катей подглядывал?
Наш Лёва запал на дочку шефа.
А что, это так заметно, да?
Я понимаю, у меня нет шансов.
Ладно, чего ты себя хоронишь?
Ты должен мне помочь с Катей.
Чего? Я не буду помогать.
Я серьёзно, ну сам посуди.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Идеальное начало дня — бодрящий душ.
'The ideal start to the day is an invigorating shower.' Max anchors the line on 'ideal', while 'shower' completes the thought.
Плотный завтрак и чашечка горячего кофе.
'A hearty breakfast and a little cup of hot coffee.' The grammar packs 'hearty' and 'coffee' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ой, Лёва, это очень горячо!
'Ouch, Lyova, that is very hot!' The meaning hinges on 'oh' working together with 'hot!' in spoken Russian. Lyova answers right away.
Прости меня, пожалуйста, я случайно.
'Forgive me, please, I did it by accident.' In Russian, the idea of 'forgive' flows naturally into 'by chance' without extra filler words.
Ты опять за Катей подглядывал?
'Were you peeking at Katya again?' Max anchors the line on 'you', while 'was peeking' completes the thought.
Наш Лёва запал на дочку шефа.
'Our Lyova has fallen for the Chef's daughter.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'our' and finishing on 'chef'. Lyova answers right away.
А что, это так заметно, да?
'Wait, is it really that noticeable?' Lyova anchors the line on 'and', while 'yes' completes the thought.
Я понимаю, у меня нет шансов.
'I understand, I do not have a chance.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'chances' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ладно, чего ты себя хоронишь?
'Come on, why are you writing yourself off?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'all right' and finishing on 'you bury'. Lyova answers right away.
Ты должен мне помочь с Катей.
'You have to help me with Katya.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'Katya'.
Чего? Я не буду помогать.
'What? I am not going to help.' The meaning hinges on 'what' working together with 'to help' in spoken Russian.
Я серьёзно, ну сам посуди.

'I am serious, just judge for yourself.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'judge for yourself' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

Я серьёзно, ну сам посуди.
Lyova is convinced that since Max brought Kostya and Nastya together, Max can work a miracle for him and Katya too. Let us hear how Max negotiates his fee.
